page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 architecture using the Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The processor includes a 35 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. It supports AVX and AVX512F vector extensions, alongside AES cryptography and FMA instructions. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and 10% respectively. Single-threaded compression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, also show poor throughput. However, the instance leverages its 16 dedicated cores to achieve average multi-core performance in stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth for both cached and uncached reads and writes remains in the average tier.

Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, the ecs.sn2ne.4xlarge is suited for multi-threaded general-purpose workloads that can distribute tasks across its 16 dedicated cores. These include static web serving, database operations, and multi-threaded decompression tasks, which all perform at average levels. It is also capable of handling light LLM inference for small models, though performance degrades on medium models. The primary tradeoff is the lower single-core efficiency, making it less optimal for single-threaded applications. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, it offers a balanced resource density for standard enterprise applications needing dedicated CPU allocation without the premium of high-frequency compute or massive memory footprints.
